title: The identity component and smooth reduction of a locally algebraic group
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure] and let $G$ be a group scheme locally of finite type over $k$ [def-sc-group-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $G^0$ denote the connected component of the identity in $|G|$ (a connected component is a maximal connected subset) [def-weil-connected-scheme]. Then $G^0$ is open and closed in $G$; with its open-subscheme structure [def-weil-open-immersion], it is a subgroup scheme, is geometrically irreducible [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], and is of finite type over $k$. Formation of $G^0$ commutes with extension of the base field. Moreover $(G^0)_{\mathrm{red}}$, the closed subscheme obtained by quotienting the structure sheaf by its nilradical [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction, def-pc-reduced-scheme], is a smooth connected integral separated group scheme of finite type over $k$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism]. It has the same underlying topological space as $G^0$.

proof.text: By pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft, $G$ is locally Noetherian, since a field is Noetherian. Apply lem-sfb-group-local-minimal-prime at each point $x$. On an affine neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $x$, write $x=\mathfrak p$. The components of $U$ through $x$ are the $V(\mathfrak q)$ for minimal primes $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak p$. The inclusion-preserving prime correspondence for $A\to A_{\mathfrak p}=\mathcal O_{G,x}$ identifies these primes with the minimal primes of that local ring: a prime strictly below one remains below $\mathfrak p$, so minimality is preserved in both directions. Thus precisely one component of $U$ contains $x$. Components of $G$ meeting $U$ inject into those of $U$ by intersection, so at most one component of $G$ contains $x$. Every point lies in some component; hence distinct components of $G$ are disjoint.

source.place: Tag 047M, lemma-group-scheme-field-geometrically-irreducible; local prime correspondence and affine component description

proof.text: The components are locally finite by lem-sc-locnoeth-components-locally-finite. Fix a component $Z$ and $x\in Z$. Choose a neighbourhood meeting only finitely many components and remove the other components meeting that neighbourhood; they are closed and none contains $x$. The remaining neighbourhood lies in $Z$. Thus all components are open, as well as closed. An irreducible component is connected, while a connected subset meeting a clopen component cannot leave it. Therefore the neutral irreducible component $Z$ is precisely $G^0$. Let $C$ be its open subscheme. Its reduction is the reduced induced closed scheme on $Z$: on an affine chart the clopen restriction followed by quotient by the nilradical gives exactly the reduced structure on that subset. By lem-sfb-group-local-minimal-prime this reduced scheme is geometrically irreducible. The reduction map $C_{\mathrm{red}}\to C$ is a universal homeomorphism, so after every field extension its source and target have homeomorphic underlying spaces. Hence $C$ itself is geometrically irreducible.

source.place: Tag 047M and proof of Tag 0B7R, proposition-connected-component; local finiteness supplies openness in the locally Noetherian case

proof.text: The product $C\times_k C$ is irreducible by lem-sc-irreducible-product-over-field. Its multiplication image is connected and contains $e$, hence lies in $C=G^0$. Inversion sends the connected set $C$ to a connected subset containing $e$, so its image also lies in $C$. The identity section has image $e\in C$. Factor these three morphisms uniquely through the open subscheme $C$ using lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme. These factorizations satisfy every group identity: composing the two sides of each identity with $C\hookrightarrow G$ gives the identity in $G$, and uniqueness of factorization through this open immersion makes the sides equal. Thus $C$ is a subgroup scheme, with its open structure, without having assumed reducedness.

source.place: Tag 0B7R, proposition-connected-component, proof: unit, inversion and multiplication factor through the neutral component

proof.text: Apply lem-sfb-irreducible-group-quasi-compact to the group scheme $C$, which is irreducible by step 2. It is quasi-compact. As an open subscheme of $G$, it is locally of finite type over $k$: at each point restrict to an affine finite-type chart lying in that open, obtained by taking a principal affine neighbourhood in a finite-type affine chart of $G$; localization $A_f$ is generated over $k$ by generators for $A$ and $f^{-1}$. Quasi-compactness chooses finitely many of these charts. Equivalently, locally of finite type plus quasi-compact is finite type, so $C/k$ is of finite type.

Let $K/k$ be any field extension. Base change of the clopen decomposition $G=C\amalg(G\setminus C)$ gives the clopen decomposition $G_K=C_K\amalg(G\setminus C)_K$, with the pullback open-subscheme structures. Since $C$ is geometrically irreducible, $C_K$ is irreducible and therefore connected, and it contains the identity $e_K$. Consequently $C_K$ lies in the connected component of $e_K$ in $G_K$. Conversely that connected component cannot meet both pieces of the clopen decomposition, so it lies in $C_K$. This proves equality of the underlying components. Their open-subscheme structures agree, being the restriction of the same structure sheaf of $G_K$. Thus $(G^0)_K=(G_K)^0$ canonically as open subgroup schemes.

source.place: Tag 0B7R, geometric irreducibility assertion, with the clopen identity-component construction

proof.text: Put $R=C_{\mathrm{red}}$ and $j:R\hookrightarrow C$. Reduction is a homeomorphism and $R$ is reduced. Therefore $R$ is connected and irreducible, hence integral by def-pc-integral-scheme. It is of finite type: the finite affine cover of $C$ induces a finite cover with rings $A/\sqrt{0}$, still finitely generated over $k$. An algebraically closed field is perfect (in characteristic $p$, every element has a root of $T^p-a$). On affine charts of $R\times_kR$ the rings are tensor products of reduced $k$-algebras, hence are reduced by lem-weil-pbc-perfect-reduced-tensor. Thus $R$, $R\times_kR$ and $\operatorname{Spec}k$ are reduced. Apply lem-weil-pbc-reduced-source-factors-through-closed-subscheme to the inverse, multiplication and unit maps into $C$ to factor them through $j$. Factorizations are unique because a closed immersion is a monomorphism; after composition with $j$ their group identities are those of $C$. Hence $R$ is a closed subgroup scheme of $C$.

source.place: Tag 047R, lemma-reduced-subgroup-scheme-perfect, including its omitted factorization argument; Tag 00I4 for reduced tensor products

proof.text: The finite-type reduced scheme $R$ over the perfect field $k$ is geometrically reduced by lem-kun-geometric-reduced-perfect. All hypotheses of lem-sfb-geometrically-reduced-group-smooth now hold: $R$ is a group scheme by step 6, is locally of finite type, and is geometrically reduced. Hence $R/k$ is smooth. Apply lem-sc-group-scheme-separated-field to $R$ to obtain separatedness. Together with step 6 this gives smoothness, connectedness, integrality, separatedness and finite type, and the reduction homeomorphism gives exactly the same underlying space as $G^0$.
